summary: Jayashree D. Sathe is a scholar in Indology and linguistics. She served at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute as editor-in-chief (attested 2011) and later as Professor-Editor for the Sanskrit Dictionary (attested 2026).

Jaś Elsner works in archaeology, history, and religious studies. He studied at Cambridge, the Courtauld Institute, London, and Harvard. His positions include the Courtauld Institute (1991–1999), Corpus Christi College, Oxford (1999), and the University of Oxford (from 2014).

Jean Boisselier (1912–1996) was a scholar of archaeology, history, and Buddhist studies who studied at the École des Beaux-Arts, École du Louvre, and the Sorbonne under Philippe Stern and Pierre Dupont. He held posts at the National Museum of Cambodia, CNRS, and Sorbonne Nouvelle University.

Jean Buhot (1885–1952) specialized in archaeology, history, Japanology, and Sinology. He was appointed Professor of Chinese and Japanese Art at the École du Louvre in 1936 and Professor of Japanese at INALCO in 1940.

Jean Carl (1900–1941) was a researcher in archaeology, history, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He held posts at the Maison Franco-Japonaise (~1934–1937) and the Délégation Archéologique Française en Afghanistan (~1937–1940).

Jean Dantinne is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Liège and KU Leuven under Étienne Lamotte. He served as a lecturer at the University of Liège in 1975 and became a professor at Université catholique de Louvain in 1983.

Jean Deloche (1929–2019) worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He taught at Suryavarman II School, directed the Alliance Française of Madras, and held long-term posts as a researcher and associate member at EFEO and the French Institute of Pondicherry.

Jean Deny (1879–1963) was a linguist specializing in Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at the Paris Faculty of Law and ENLOV, he held posts at the French Ministry of Foreign Affairs, ENLOV (1908–1948), and Georgetown University (1949–1953).

Jean Ferdinand Caius (1877–1944) was an Indology scholar who studied at St. Mary's College, Kurseong, St Beuno's, and the University of Paris. He taught at St. Joseph's College, worked as a pharmacologist at the Haffkine Institute, and researched at St. Xavier's College, Mumbai.

Jean Filliozat (1906–1982) was an Indologist and historian educated at EPHE and the University of Paris under Sylvain Lévi and Louis Renou. He held professorships at EPHE and the Collège de France, and directed both EFEO and the French Institute of Pondicherry.

Jean Haudry (1934–2023) was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. Educated at the École Normale Supérieure, Sorbonne Nouvelle, and under Armand Minard, he held academic posts at EPHE (~1967–2002) and Jean Moulin University - Lyon 3 (~1974–2002).

Jean Herbert (1897–1980) was a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied under Sri Aurobindo. Beyond roles at the League of Nations, Éditions Albin Michel, and the United Nations, he taught Eastern Mythologies at the University of Geneva (1954–1964).

Jean Kellens (born 1944) is a scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, Indological, and linguistic studies. He studied at the University of Liège and under Karl Hoffmann at Erlangen-Nuremberg, later holding posts at Mainz, Liège, and the Collège de France (1993).

Jean Petitot (born 1944) works in philosophy and linguistics. A former student of the École Polytechnique, he later served as a director there (~1992–2006) and held a post at the School for Advanced Studies in the Social Sciences (~1980).

Jean Philippe Vogel (1871–1958) was an Indologist and archaeologist who studied at the University of Amsterdam under Johan Kern and C. C. Uhlenbeck. He served in the Archaeological Survey of India (1901–1914) and as a director at Leiden University (1914–1939).

Jean Przyluski (1885–1944) was a Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics scholar who studied at EPHE and ENFOM under Sylvain Lévi and Antoine Meillet. He held chairs at INALCO (1913–1933), EPHE (1926–1944), and the Collège de France (1930–1944).

Jean Varenne (1926–1997) was an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied at EPHE and under Jean Haudry. He held posts at Savitribai Phule Pune University, Aix-Marseille University (1962–1980), and Jean Moulin University Lyon 3 (1981–1987).

Jean-Antoine Dubois (1765–1848) was an Indology and religious studies scholar educated at Collège de Bourg-Saint-Andéol and the MEP. He directed the Seminary of Pondicherry (1813–1819) and later served as supérieur of the Paris Foreign Missions Society in 1836.

Jean-Baptiste Biot (1774–1862) was a scholar in history, Indology, and science. Educated at École des Ponts and École Polytechnique under Gaspard Monge and Pierre-Simon Laplace, he held professorships at Beauvais, the Collège de France (1800–1862), and the University of Paris (1809).

Jean-Denis Lanjuinais (1753–1827) was a scholar in Indology and religious studies who earned a doctorate of laws at the University of Rennes in 1771. He became Professor of Canonic Law there in 1775 and joined the Académie des Inscriptions et Belles-Lettres in 1808.
